title: Sunny and the Wallaby Joey | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka meets a tiny wallaby joey peeking out from his mother's warm pouch for the very first time, gazing up at the night sky with wide, wondering eyes. A gentle and heartwarming bedtime tale from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The moon was up, big and round and pale, like a soft lamp hung in the sky. Little Sonny the quokka was wandering through the quiet bush, her paws whispering across the cool night grass.

Then she stopped. There, beneath a silver gum tree, stood a mother wallaby. She was very still and very gentle, her long ears tipped forward. And tucked inside her soft warm pouch was the tiniest face Sunny had ever seen.

Two enormous dark eyes blinked out from the pouch. A little pink nose twitched. The joey was so small, so new. This was his very first night of peeking out at the world.

Sunny crept closer, very slowly and very quietly, so as not to startle him. The joey's eyes grew wide. He looked up — up past his mother's soft grey chest, past the top of the gum tree — and saw the sky. All those stars. That big round moon.

His tiny mouth fell open. Just a little. Sunny watched him take it all in, his huge eyes reflecting every star, one by one.

Sunny sat down in the soft grass beside them and looked up too. The stars really were something, she thought. She had seen them many times. But to see them for the very first time — that must feel like a wonderful surprise.

The joey yawned, the tiniest yawn, and slowly tucked his head back into the warm, dark pouch. The mother wallaby looked down at Sunny with soft, calm eyes.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little joey. Goodnight, little one.
